hooks.text: A massive star is rocketing through space as a celestial fugitive.
Why is a dying giant star plowing through the galaxy at thirty kilometers per second?
A runaway star is plowing through space at thirty kilometers per second.

title: The Runaway Giant Star Plowing Through Space
description: Discover Betelgeuse, a runaway star flung from its birthplace near Orion's Belt, creating a massive bow shock as it plows through space.

beats.text: A massive star is rocketing through space as a celestial fugitive.
Betelgeuse is a red supergiant star located in the constellation of Orion.
beats.visual: Hubble Space Telescope direct image of Betelgeuse disk, 2010
queries: Betelgeuse Hubble Space Telescope direct image

beats.text: If placed at the center of the solar system, it would engulf the orbits of Mercury, Venus, Earth, and Mars.
beats.visual: Solar system vs Betelgeuse orbit illustration, 2018
queries: Solar system vs Betelgeuse orbit illustration

beats.text: This ancient giant is a runaway star that was ejected from its birthplace near the stars in Orion's Belt.
The star is moving through space at a speed of thirty kilometers per second.
beats.visual: Artist impression of a runaway star's bow shock, 2012

beats.text: Its movement creates a massive bow shock where its stellar wind crashes into the interstellar medium.
beats.visual: Akari infrared survey image of Betelgeuse bow shock, 2012

beats.text: This shockwave stretches roughly three to four light-years wide in front of the fleeing giant.
beats.visual: Infrared image of Betelgeuse bow shock by Akari, 2012

beats.text: That is why a massive star is rocketing through space as a celestial fugitive.
beats.visual: Artist impression of Betelgeuse and bow shock, 2015
